question: What is usually the largest energy use in a water distribution utility?
correctAnswer: Pumping water through the distribution system
explanation: Pumping moves the entire volume of water supplied, so pumping energy normally dominates a distribution utility energy bill.
options: Pumping water through the distribution system
Lighting at administrative offices
Heating small valve chambers
Powering handheld field radios
optionA: Pumping water through the distribution system
optionB: Lighting at administrative offices
optionC: Heating small valve chambers
optionD: Powering handheld field radios
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy Strategy for Pumping. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Support Systems: Energy Strategy for Pumping

question: Why do many utilities schedule major pumping during off peak electricity periods?
correctAnswer: To reduce electricity cost while still filling storage
explanation: Storage filled during lower cost off peak periods can supply peak demand later, reducing electricity cost without reducing service.
options: To increase water age in storage tanks
To avoid disinfectant residual testing
To reduce electricity cost while still filling storage
To raise distribution pressure above its normal limit
optionA: To increase water age in storage tanks
optionB: To avoid disinfectant residual testing
optionC: To reduce electricity cost while still filling storage
optionD: To raise distribution pressure above its normal limit
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy Strategy for Pumping. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Support Systems: Energy Strategy for Pumping

question: What does a pump efficiency test compare?
correctAnswer: The energy used with the useful hydraulic work delivered
explanation: Efficiency compares useful hydraulic output with energy input, so a falling efficiency means more energy is used for the same work.
options: The age of the pump with the age of its motor
The number of starts with the number of stops
The colour of the pump with its nameplate rating
The energy used with the useful hydraulic work delivered
optionA: The age of the pump with the age of its motor
optionB: The number of starts with the number of stops
optionC: The colour of the pump with its nameplate rating
optionD: The energy used with the useful hydraulic work delivered
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy Strategy for Pumping. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Support Systems: Energy Strategy for Pumping

question: How does storage support efficient pumping?
correctAnswer: Pumps can run steadily at efficient rates while storage meets short term demand peaks
explanation: Storage decouples pumping from moment to moment demand, letting pumps run longer at steady, efficient operating points.
options: Pumps can run steadily at efficient rates while storage meets short term demand peaks
Storage removes the need to monitor pump performance
Storage allows pumps to run only when a tank is empty
Storage eliminates leakage from the distribution system
optionA: Pumps can run steadily at efficient rates while storage meets short term demand peaks
optionB: Storage removes the need to monitor pump performance
optionC: Storage allows pumps to run only when a tank is empty
optionD: Storage eliminates leakage from the distribution system
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy Strategy for Pumping. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Support Systems: Energy Strategy for Pumping

question: How does reducing leakage support an energy strategy?
correctAnswer: Less water must be pumped to deliver the same consumption
explanation: Every litre lost to leakage was pumped at full energy cost, so loss reduction cuts pumping energy for the same delivered demand.
options: Less water must be pumped to deliver the same consumption
It increases the volume that must be pumped each day
It removes the need for pressure management
It raises the disinfectant residual in storage
optionA: Less water must be pumped to deliver the same consumption
optionB: It increases the volume that must be pumped each day
optionC: It removes the need for pressure management
optionD: It raises the disinfectant residual in storage
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy Strategy for Pumping. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Support Systems: Energy Strategy for Pumping

question: What is the main purpose of a multi year capital plan?
correctAnswer: To identify major projects, their timing, and how they will be funded
explanation: A capital plan looks several years ahead, sequencing major projects and matching them to funding so renewal and growth are not left to chance.
options: To record daily operator log entries
To set the chlorine dose for the next shift
To identify major projects, their timing, and how they will be funded
To schedule vacation coverage for operations staff
optionA: To record daily operator log entries
optionB: To set the chlorine dose for the next shift
optionC: To identify major projects, their timing, and how they will be funded
optionD: To schedule vacation coverage for operations staff
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Capital Planning Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: How should asset condition information be used in capital planning?
correctAnswer: To prioritize renewal where failure risk and consequence are highest
explanation: Condition and criticality together show where failure is most likely and most damaging, which is where renewal dollars do the most work.
options: To prioritize renewal where failure risk and consequence are highest
To renew the newest assets first
To postpone all renewal until assets fail
To replace assets in the order they were purchased
optionA: To prioritize renewal where failure risk and consequence are highest
optionB: To renew the newest assets first
optionC: To postpone all renewal until assets fail
optionD: To replace assets in the order they were purchased
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Capital Planning Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What does a lifecycle cost view of an asset include?
correctAnswer: Acquisition, operation, maintenance, renewal, and eventual disposal
explanation: Lifecycle costing counts the full cost of owning an asset over its life, not just the price paid to acquire it.
options: Only the original purchase price
Only the cost of the first year of operation
Purchase price plus a contingency allowance only
Acquisition, operation, maintenance, renewal, and eventual disposal
optionA: Only the original purchase price
optionB: Only the cost of the first year of operation
optionC: Purchase price plus a contingency allowance only
optionD: Acquisition, operation, maintenance, renewal, and eventual disposal
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Capital Planning Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which of the following is a capital funding source for a distribution utility?
correctAnswer: A dedicated capital reserve funded from water rates
explanation: Reserves built from rates are a standard way to fund capital work, while chemicals and overtime are operating costs.
options: A dedicated capital reserve funded from water rates
The daily chemical delivery invoice
A routine hydrant flushing record
An operator overtime request form
optionA: A dedicated capital reserve funded from water rates
optionB: The daily chemical delivery invoice
optionC: A routine hydrant flushing record
optionD: An operator overtime request form
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Capital Planning Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why are growth projects identified separately from renewal projects in a capital plan?
correctAnswer: So expansion costs and their funding are not hidden inside renewal needs
explanation: Separating growth from renewal keeps each need visible, so the funding source and priority for each can be judged on its own merits.
options: So expansion costs and their funding are not hidden inside renewal needs
So growth projects never require approval
So renewal projects can be charged to developers
So growth assets do not need to meet design standards
optionA: So expansion costs and their funding are not hidden inside renewal needs
optionB: So growth projects never require approval
optionC: So renewal projects can be charged to developers
optionD: So growth assets do not need to meet design standards
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Capital Planning Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is the main purpose of a booster disinfection program?
correctAnswer: To restore disinfectant residual in areas where it has decayed with water age
explanation: Residual decays as water travels and ages, so booster stations add disinfectant at selected points to restore the residual where it is needed.
options: To restore disinfectant residual in areas where it has decayed with water age
To replace the primary disinfection process at the treatment plant
To increase the pressure in low pressure zones
To remove sediment from the inside of water mains
optionA: To restore disinfectant residual in areas where it has decayed with water age
optionB: To replace the primary disinfection process at the treatment plant
optionC: To increase the pressure in low pressure zones
optionD: To remove sediment from the inside of water mains
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Booster Disinfection Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A pressure district far from the treatment plant consistently shows low residual at its far end while the rest of the system is compliant. What is the best leadership response?
correctAnswer: Evaluate a booster station serving that district
explanation: A localized low residual problem is best solved locally with booster disinfection, rather than overdosing the entire system from the plant.
options: Raise the plant dose until the whole system carries a high residual
Stop sampling the far end of the district
Evaluate a booster station serving that district
Flush the district once and close the file
optionA: Raise the plant dose until the whole system carries a high residual
optionB: Stop sampling the far end of the district
optionC: Evaluate a booster station serving that district
optionD: Flush the district once and close the file
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Booster Disinfection Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is a key risk of overdosing disinfectant at a booster station?
correctAnswer: Taste and odour complaints and greater disinfection byproduct formation potential
explanation: Excess disinfectant can create taste and odour complaints and can increase disinfection byproduct formation, so dosing must be controlled to a target.
options: Loss of pressure in the booster zone
Immediate failure of the booster pump seals
Freezing of the chemical feed line in summer
Taste and odour complaints and greater disinfection byproduct formation potential
optionA: Loss of pressure in the booster zone
optionB: Immediate failure of the booster pump seals
optionC: Freezing of the chemical feed line in summer
optionD: Taste and odour complaints and greater disinfection byproduct formation potential
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Booster Disinfection Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: How should a booster program verify that its dosing is working as intended?
correctAnswer: By tracking residual upstream and downstream of the booster point against a target
explanation: Upstream and downstream residual results show whether the added dose reaches the target in the zone without excess.
options: By checking the chemical tank level once a month
By counting the number of customer calls received
By replacing the feed pump on a fixed schedule
By tracking residual upstream and downstream of the booster point against a target
optionA: By checking the chemical tank level once a month
optionB: By counting the number of customer calls received
optionC: By replacing the feed pump on a fixed schedule
optionD: By tracking residual upstream and downstream of the booster point against a target
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Booster Disinfection Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why does tank mixing matter when disinfectant is boosted at a storage facility?
correctAnswer: Good mixing distributes the added disinfectant so it does not short circuit or leave stratified zones
explanation: Without mixing, added disinfectant can short circuit to the outlet or leave poorly mixed zones with low residual inside the same tank.
options: Mixing prevents the booster chemical from being measured
Mixing removes the need for residual sampling at the tank
Mixing increases the volume of water stored in the tank
Good mixing distributes the added disinfectant so it does not short circuit or leave stratified zones
optionA: Mixing prevents the booster chemical from being measured
optionB: Mixing removes the need for residual sampling at the tank
optionC: Mixing increases the volume of water stored in the tank
optionD: Good mixing distributes the added disinfectant so it does not short circuit or leave stratified zones
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Booster Disinfection Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: During a major water main break with widespread pressure loss, what is the first leadership priority?
correctAnswer: Protecting public health and isolating the affected area
explanation: Public health protection and isolation of the affected area come first, because pressure loss can allow contamination into the system.
options: Completing the repair cost estimate
Preparing a media statement about the contractor
Replacing the broken section before assessing the impact
Protecting public health and isolating the affected area
optionA: Completing the repair cost estimate
optionB: Preparing a media statement about the contractor
optionC: Replacing the broken section before assessing the impact
optionD: Protecting public health and isolating the affected area
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Emergency Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why does an emergency plan assign roles and decision authority in advance?
correctAnswer: So the response does not wait for ad hoc organization during the event
explanation: Preassigned roles and authority let staff act immediately and in coordination instead of spending the first hours deciding who is in charge.
options: So the response does not wait for ad hoc organization during the event
So no records need to be kept during an emergency
So only one person may speak to operations staff
So mutual aid is never required from other utilities
optionA: So the response does not wait for ad hoc organization during the event
optionB: So no records need to be kept during an emergency
optionC: So only one person may speak to operations staff
optionD: So mutual aid is never required from other utilities
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Emergency Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: When pressure loss creates a contamination risk in part of a system, how is a precautionary drinking water advisory handled?
correctAnswer: It follows regulatory and public health direction for the affected area
explanation: Advisories are a public health measure taken under regulatory and public health direction when contamination risk cannot be ruled out.
options: The crew foreman issues it without notifying anyone
It is avoided so customers are not alarmed
It is issued only after the next scheduled sampling round
It follows regulatory and public health direction for the affected area
optionA: The crew foreman issues it without notifying anyone
optionB: It is avoided so customers are not alarmed
optionC: It is issued only after the next scheduled sampling round
optionD: It follows regulatory and public health direction for the affected area
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Emergency Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What do prearranged mutual aid agreements give a utility during a large emergency?
correctAnswer: Access to crews, equipment, and materials from neighbouring utilities
explanation: Mutual aid agreements arranged in advance let neighbouring utilities provide people, equipment, and materials quickly when an event exceeds local capacity.
options: Permission to skip required water quality sampling
A guarantee that no advisory will be needed
Exemption from reporting the incident
Access to crews, equipment, and materials from neighbouring utilities
optionA: Permission to skip required water quality sampling
optionB: A guarantee that no advisory will be needed
optionC: Exemption from reporting the incident
optionD: Access to crews, equipment, and materials from neighbouring utilities
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Emergency Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What should an after action review following a major incident produce?
correctAnswer: A list of findings with corrective actions, owners, and completion dates
explanation: An after action review only improves readiness when its findings become assigned corrective actions that are tracked to completion.
options: A decision that no changes are needed
A summary kept only by the person who led the response
A replacement emergency plan written by one operator
A list of findings with corrective actions, owners, and completion dates
optionA: A decision that no changes are needed
optionB: A summary kept only by the person who led the response
optionC: A replacement emergency plan written by one operator
optionD: A list of findings with corrective actions, owners, and completion dates
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Emergency Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What does inspection readiness leadership mean in practice?
correctAnswer: Keeping records, procedures, and staff knowledge current every day
explanation: A system that is run in a documented, compliant way every day is ready for inspection at any time, not just on a scheduled date.
options: Assembling records in the week before an inspector arrives
Limiting inspections to one area of the operation
Asking the inspector to accept verbal summaries instead of records
Keeping records, procedures, and staff knowledge current every day
optionA: Assembling records in the week before an inspector arrives
optionB: Limiting inspections to one area of the operation
optionC: Asking the inspector to accept verbal summaries instead of records
optionD: Keeping records, procedures, and staff knowledge current every day
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Inspection Readiness Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why must operating procedures and records be readily accessible to distribution staff?
correctAnswer: So staff can find and follow them during operations and show them during an inspection
explanation: Procedures and records that staff cannot reach cannot guide the work or demonstrate compliance when an inspector asks for them.
options: So staff can find and follow them during operations and show them during an inspection
So they can be stored in a single locked office
So only managers are able to review them
So procedures do not need to be updated
optionA: So staff can find and follow them during operations and show them during an inspection
optionB: So they can be stored in a single locked office
optionC: So only managers are able to review them
optionD: So procedures do not need to be updated
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Inspection Readiness Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What should sampling records show when an inspector reviews them?
correctAnswer: Sampling results with any adverse result follow up fully documented
explanation: Complete records, including how adverse results were responded to, demonstrate both the sampling program and the corrective action system.
options: Only the samples that met every requirement
The names of the staff who were on vacation
Sampling results with any adverse result follow up fully documented
A total count with no individual results
optionA: Only the samples that met every requirement
optionB: The names of the staff who were on vacation
optionC: Sampling results with any adverse result follow up fully documented
optionD: A total count with no individual results
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Inspection Readiness Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: How should operators be prepared for inspection interviews?
correctAnswer: They should be able to explain the procedures they actually perform and where the records are kept
explanation: Inspectors test whether the documented system is the real system, so operators need to explain their own work and records confidently.
options: They should memorize a script written by management
They should only discuss work done by other departments
They should be able to explain the procedures they actually perform and where the records are kept
They should refer every question to the inspector in writing
optionA: They should memorize a script written by management
optionB: They should only discuss work done by other departments
optionC: They should be able to explain the procedures they actually perform and where the records are kept
optionD: They should refer every question to the inspector in writing
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Inspection Readiness Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: How should findings from audits and inspections be managed to closure?
correctAnswer: They are tracked with assigned actions and evidence that each corrective action worked
explanation: Tracking findings to closure, with evidence the fix worked, prevents the same finding from returning at the next inspection.
options: They are filed once the inspection report is received
They are tracked with assigned actions and evidence that each corrective action worked
They are closed when the next inspection is scheduled
They are assigned to whichever operator was interviewed
optionA: They are filed once the inspection report is received
optionB: They are tracked with assigned actions and evidence that each corrective action worked
optionC: They are closed when the next inspection is scheduled
optionD: They are assigned to whichever operator was interviewed
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Inspection Readiness Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is the purpose of unidirectional flushing?
correctAnswer: To scour mains at a controlled velocity in one direction, removing sediment and improving water quality
explanation: Unidirectional flushing isolates a path and moves water one way at scouring velocity, carrying loosened sediment out through a hydrant.
options: To push water in both directions at once to save time
To scour mains at a controlled velocity in one direction, removing sediment and improving water quality
To empty a storage tank as quickly as possible
To test hydrant caps for leaks
optionA: To push water in both directions at once to save time
optionB: To scour mains at a controlled velocity in one direction, removing sediment and improving water quality
optionC: To empty a storage tank as quickly as possible
optionD: To test hydrant caps for leaks
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing and Turnover Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: In what sequence should a unidirectional flushing program normally proceed?
correctAnswer: From clean areas near the source outward to the areas with poorer quality
explanation: Starting clean and working outward prevents loosened material from being pushed into mains that have already been cleaned.
options: From the dirtiest dead ends back toward the plant
Randomly, wherever a crew is available
From clean areas near the source outward to the areas with poorer quality
From the highest pressure zone to the lowest, regardless of quality
optionA: From the dirtiest dead ends back toward the plant
optionB: Randomly, wherever a crew is available
optionC: From clean areas near the source outward to the areas with poorer quality
optionD: From the highest pressure zone to the lowest, regardless of quality
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing and Turnover Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: How does regular flushing of dead end mains support water quality?
correctAnswer: It reduces water age and helps maintain disinfectant residual
explanation: Dead ends have little natural turnover, so scheduled flushing replaces aged water with fresher water and supports the residual.
options: It reduces water age and helps maintain disinfectant residual
It increases the pressure at the dead end permanently
It removes the need for residual sampling at dead ends
It prevents any sediment from ever forming again
optionA: It reduces water age and helps maintain disinfectant residual
optionB: It increases the pressure at the dead end permanently
optionC: It removes the need for residual sampling at dead ends
optionD: It prevents any sediment from ever forming again
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing and Turnover Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which evidence best shows whether a flushing program is improving quality in a problem area?
correctAnswer: Before and after residual and clarity results in that area
explanation: Program success is judged by measured quality change in the target area, not by activity counts or water volume alone.
options: The number of hydrants opened during the program
The total volume of water used in a season
Before and after residual and clarity results in that area
The age of the flushing crew equipment
optionA: The number of hydrants opened during the program
optionB: The total volume of water used in a season
optionC: Before and after residual and clarity results in that area
optionD: The age of the flushing crew equipment
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing and Turnover Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What should leadership arrange before a planned flushing program on residential streets?
correctAnswer: Advance public notice, because flushing can cause temporary discoloured water
explanation: Advance notice prepares customers for temporary discolouration and reduces complaint calls while the program is underway.
options: Advance public notice, because flushing can cause temporary discoloured water
A boil water advisory for the whole system
Closure of every business on the affected streets
Removal of all water meters on the affected streets
optionA: Advance public notice, because flushing can cause temporary discoloured water
optionB: A boil water advisory for the whole system
optionC: Closure of every business on the affected streets
optionD: Removal of all water meters on the affected streets
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing and Turnover Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why should a utility avoid taking several storage tanks out of service in the same period?
correctAnswer: Simultaneous outages reduce available storage and system resilience if demand or an emergency rises
explanation: Staggering tank outages preserves storage for fire protection, emergencies, and peak demand while individual tanks are inspected or repaired.
options: Tank inspections are not permitted in the same season
Simultaneous outages reduce available storage and system resilience if demand or an emergency rises
Tanks taken out together must all be replaced
It prevents operators from sampling the remaining tanks
optionA: Tank inspections are not permitted in the same season
optionB: Simultaneous outages reduce available storage and system resilience if demand or an emergency rises
optionC: Tanks taken out together must all be replaced
optionD: It prevents operators from sampling the remaining tanks
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Storage Fleet Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: How should a tank inspection program prioritize a fleet of storage facilities?
correctAnswer: By condition, coating history, and the consequence of an outage at each site
explanation: Prioritization weighs the likelihood of deterioration against the impact of taking that tank out of service, so limited funds address the highest risk first.
options: By age alone, oldest first in every case
By the order in which tanks were painted
By condition, coating history, and the consequence of an outage at each site
By choosing the tanks that are easiest to reach
optionA: By age alone, oldest first in every case
optionB: By the order in which tanks were painted
optionC: By condition, coating history, and the consequence of an outage at each site
optionD: By choosing the tanks that are easiest to reach
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Storage Fleet Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A utility wants faster tank turnover to reduce water age, but one tank provides most of the fire storage for its zone. What is the correct leadership decision?
correctAnswer: Increase turnover only within limits that preserve the required emergency and fire storage
explanation: Turnover improvements must be balanced against the storage the zone depends on for fire protection and emergencies, which sets a floor on operating levels.
options: Drain the tank lower every day regardless of fire storage needs
Increase turnover only within limits that preserve the required emergency and fire storage
Stop monitoring water age in that zone
Remove the tank from service permanently
optionA: Drain the tank lower every day regardless of fire storage needs
optionB: Increase turnover only within limits that preserve the required emergency and fire storage
optionC: Stop monitoring water age in that zone
optionD: Remove the tank from service permanently
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Storage Fleet Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Several tanks in a fleet share the same level control design, and one fails in service. What fleet level lesson should leadership draw?
correctAnswer: A common design can carry a common failure mode, so alarms and independent high level protection should be standardized across the fleet
explanation: A failure in a shared design is a warning about the whole fleet, so protective measures should be applied consistently, not just at the failed site.
options: Only the failed tank needs attention, since failures are always isolated
A common design can carry a common failure mode, so alarms and independent high level protection should be standardized across the fleet
Level controls should be removed from the other tanks
The fleet should be operated without level alarms until the next budget year
optionA: Only the failed tank needs attention, since failures are always isolated
optionB: A common design can carry a common failure mode, so alarms and independent high level protection should be standardized across the fleet
optionC: Level controls should be removed from the other tanks
optionD: The fleet should be operated without level alarms until the next budget year
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Storage Fleet Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which information belongs in the asset register for a storage fleet so capital work can be planned?
correctAnswer: Coating condition, structural findings, and cleaning and inspection history for each tank
explanation: Condition and history records let planners forecast coating, structural, and cleaning work across the fleet instead of reacting tank by tank.
options: Only the original construction cost of each tank
Coating condition, structural findings, and cleaning and inspection history for each tank
The names of the crews who last visited each site
Daily tank levels for the current week only
optionA: Only the original construction cost of each tank
optionB: Coating condition, structural findings, and cleaning and inspection history for each tank
optionC: The names of the crews who last visited each site
optionD: Daily tank levels for the current week only
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Storage Fleet Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is the accountability of the Overall Responsible Operator in an Ontario drinking water system?
correctAnswer: Overall operational responsibility for the system, even though individual tasks are delegated to other operators
explanation: The ORO carries overall responsibility for the operation of the system, which is why delegation of tasks does not remove that accountability.
options: The ORO is accountable only for the shifts they personally work
Overall operational responsibility for the system, even though individual tasks are delegated to other operators
Accountability limited to reviewing sampling results once a year
Responsibility only for systems with more than one treatment plant
optionA: The ORO is accountable only for the shifts they personally work
optionB: Overall operational responsibility for the system, even though individual tasks are delegated to other operators
optionC: Accountability limited to reviewing sampling results once a year
optionD: Responsibility only for systems with more than one treatment plant
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: ORO Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: An ORO delegates a critical operating task to another operator. What must the ORO ensure?
correctAnswer: That the operator is properly certified and competent for the task, with clear authority to act
explanation: Delegation works when the person is certified and competent for the task and knows their authority, while accountability stays with the ORO.
options: That the task no longer appears in any operating record
That the operator is properly certified and competent for the task, with clear authority to act
That the operator accepts the ORO accountability in writing
That the task is performed only when the ORO is on site
optionA: That the task no longer appears in any operating record
optionB: That the operator is properly certified and competent for the task, with clear authority to act
optionC: That the operator accepts the ORO accountability in writing
optionD: That the task is performed only when the ORO is on site
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: ORO Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: During an adverse water quality incident, what is the ORO leadership role?
correctAnswer: To ensure the prescribed corrective actions, notifications, and documentation happen and to verify completion
explanation: The ORO ensures the required response actually happens, that notifications are made, and that completion is verified and documented.
options: To wait for the next business day before acting
To personally perform every corrective action alone
To ensure the prescribed corrective actions, notifications, and documentation happen and to verify completion
To decide whether the incident needs to be reported at all
optionA: To wait for the next business day before acting
optionB: To personally perform every corrective action alone
optionC: To ensure the prescribed corrective actions, notifications, and documentation happen and to verify completion
optionD: To decide whether the incident needs to be reported at all
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: ORO Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why does a utility need planned backup coverage for the ORO role?
correctAnswer: So ORO duties continue during absences, with a designated qualified person able to act
explanation: ORO duties do not pause for illness or vacation, so qualified backup coverage must be designated in advance.
options: So the ORO never has to attend management meetings
So ORO duties continue during absences, with a designated qualified person able to act
So two people can hold the role with no clear accountability
So certification requirements can be waived during vacations
optionA: So the ORO never has to attend management meetings
optionB: So ORO duties continue during absences, with a designated qualified person able to act
optionC: So two people can hold the role with no clear accountability
optionD: So certification requirements can be waived during vacations
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: ORO Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What should the ORO bring into a management review of the drinking water quality management system?
correctAnswer: Operational risks, incident lessons, and resource needs, so decisions and resources follow from them
explanation: Management review is where operational risk and resource needs reach decision makers, and the ORO is the voice of operations in that room.
options: Only the financial results for the previous quarter
Operational risks, incident lessons, and resource needs, so decisions and resources follow from them
A list of operators requesting schedule changes
The names of suppliers used in the previous year
optionA: Only the financial results for the previous quarter
optionB: Operational risks, incident lessons, and resource needs, so decisions and resources follow from them
